notes.我们: 我 “I” + 们 (plural people suffix) → we/us.
notes.什么: A question word meaning “what”. Its modern meaning cannot be obtained by adding the standalone senses of 什 and 么.
notes.没有: 没 negates 有 “have”: not have; also used to negate completed actions.
notes.自己: 自 and 己 both point to the self; together they mean oneself.
notes.战国策: A book title: 战国 is the Warring States period; 策 refers to strategies or records. The title means Strategies of the Warring States.
notes.分钟: 分 is a time division and 钟 refers to clock time; together 分钟 means minute(s).
notes.四十分钟: 四十 = four tens (40); 分钟 = minutes. This highlight is a phrase, not a single dictionary word.
notes.一本书: 一 = one; 本 is the measure word for books; 书 = book. Together: a/one book.
notes.听完: 听 “listen” + 完 “finish”: finish listening. 完 is a result complement.
notes.太后: A historical title for an emperor’s or king’s mother: the queen/empress dowager. 后 here is a royal title, not “after”.
notes.长安君: A title, Lord Chang’an: 长安 is the place/title name and 君 means lord. It should not be translated by adding dictionary senses.
notes.狐假虎威: Literally, a fox borrows a tiger’s authority. Figuratively: intimidate others by relying on someone else’s power.
notes.亡羊补牢: Literally, mend the pen after losing sheep. Figuratively: take remedial action after a loss to prevent further harm.
notes.画蛇添足: Literally, draw a snake and add feet. Figuratively: spoil something by adding an unnecessary extra.
notes.惊弓之鸟: Literally, a bird frightened by a bow. Figuratively: someone made fearful by an earlier bad experience.
notes.南辕北辙: Literally, the cart shafts point south but its tracks lead north. Figuratively: actions run counter to the intended goal.
notes.狡兔三窟: Literally, a crafty rabbit has three burrows. Figuratively: keep several refuges or fallback plans.
notes.门庭若市: Literally, the entrance and courtyard are like a marketplace. Figuratively: a constant stream of visitors.
notes.图穷匕现: Literally, when the map is unrolled to its end, the dagger appears. Figuratively: a hidden plot or intention is finally exposed.
notes.对牛弹琴: Literally, play the qin to an ox. Figuratively: address someone who cannot understand or appreciate what you are saying.
notes.高枕无忧: Literally, rest on a high pillow without worry. Figuratively: feel secure and free of concern.
notes.得寸进尺: Literally, gain an inch and then advance a foot. Figuratively: become increasingly demanding after a concession.
notes.远交近攻: Literally, befriend the distant and attack the nearby: form alliances with distant states while attacking neighboring ones.
notes.合纵连横: Historical alliance strategies: 合纵 coordinated states against Qin; 连横 involved separate alliances with Qin. 纵 and 横 evoke vertical and horizontal groupings.
notes.杀鸡儆猴: Literally, kill a chicken to warn the monkeys. Figuratively: punish one person as a warning to others.
notes.绨袍之义: Literally, the kindness of a coarse-silk robe. Refers here to the small act of kindness shown when Xu Jia gave Fan Ju a robe.
notes.悬梁刺股: Literally, hang one’s hair from a beam and prick one’s thigh. An allusion to extreme determination in studying.
notes.投机取巧: 投机 means exploit an opportunity; 取巧 means use a clever shortcut. Together: seek an easy advantage, often unscrupulously.
notes.道貌岸然: A dignified, solemn outward appearance, often used critically for someone pretending to be morally upright.
notes.咬牙切齿: Literally, clench the teeth and grind them. Figuratively: express intense anger or hatred.
notes.一事无成: Literally, not even one affair is accomplished. Figuratively: achieve nothing.
notes.身无分文: Literally, have not a fraction of a coin on one’s person. Figuratively: be penniless.
notes.荣华富贵: 荣华 evokes flourishing splendor; 富贵 wealth and rank. Together: prosperity, wealth and high status.
notes.功高震主: Literally, achievements so great that they shake the ruler. A subordinate’s success makes the ruler feel threatened.
notes.扶老携幼: Literally, support the old and lead the young by the hand. Describes a whole family or community on the move.
notes.蝇头小利: Literally, tiny gains like a fly’s head. Figuratively: a paltry profit.
notes.隐姓埋名: Literally, conceal one’s surname and bury one’s name. Figuratively: hide one’s identity.
notes.家破人亡: Literally, the home is destroyed and people die. Describes a family ruined by disaster.
notes.魂飞魄散: Literally, the soul flies away and the spirit scatters. Figuratively: be terrified out of one’s wits.
notes.走投无路: Literally, have no road to turn to. Figuratively: be at the end of one’s resources.
notes.千刀万剐: Literally, a thousand cuts and ten thousand slices. Evokes an extremely cruel punishment or intense desire for revenge.
notes.不可思议: Literally, cannot be conceived or discussed. In ordinary modern use: inconceivable; astonishing.
notes.尔虞我诈: Literally, you deceive and I cheat. Figuratively: mutual deception and intrigue.
notes.背信弃义: Literally, turn one’s back on trust and abandon righteousness. Figuratively: betray a promise or act treacherously.
notes.见利忘义: Literally, see profit and forget righteousness. Figuratively: sacrifice principles for gain.
notes.唇枪舌剑: Literally, lips are spears and tongues are swords. Figuratively: a sharp verbal battle.
notes.和颜悦色: Literally, a gentle face and a pleasing expression. Figuratively: speak or behave in a kind, affable manner.
notes.春风得意: Literally, feel pleased in the spring breeze. Figuratively: enjoy success and feel elated.
notes.铜墙铁壁: Literally, copper walls and iron ramparts. Figuratively: an exceptionally strong defense.
notes.一兵一卒: Literally, one soldier and one foot soldier. Often negated to mean not a single soldier.
notes.千山万水: Literally, a thousand mountains and ten thousand rivers. Figuratively: a long, difficult journey.
notes.头破血流: Literally, the head is split and blood flows. Can describe severe injury or a disastrous clash.
notes.牛屁股吗: This saved highlight includes 吗, a question particle. It is a phrase fragment, not one compound word.
notes.须贾一: This saved highlight crosses a word boundary: 须贾 is the personal name Xu Jia; 一 begins the following expression. Read them separately.
